questions.stem: Why is methane measured in CO2 equivalent (CO2e) when calculating carbon footprints?

options.text: Because methane is actually a form of carbon dioxide
Because different greenhouse gases have different warming potentials, so they are converted to a common unit for comparison
Because methane is too difficult to measure directly
Because methane and carbon dioxide are always released together

questions.explanation: Different greenhouse gases trap different amounts of heat. Methane is about 25 times more potent than CO2 as a greenhouse gas, and nitrous oxide is about 300 times more potent. Converting all gases to CO2 equivalent allows meaningful comparison and a single total figure for carbon footprint.

questions.stem: What is the main criticism of carbon offsetting as a strategy to tackle climate change?

options.text: It is illegal in most countries
It does not actually reduce the emissions produced and can be used as an excuse not to cut emissions directly
It only works for transport emissions
It is too expensive for anyone to use

questions.explanation: While carbon offsetting funds projects that reduce CO2 elsewhere (such as tree planting), it does not reduce the original emissions. Critics argue it can be used as 'greenwashing' - an excuse to continue polluting rather than making real reductions. The best approach is to reduce emissions first, then offset the remainder.
